    "ÿ": "y", "ß": "ss", "ć": "c", "č": "c", "đ": "d",
    "ę": "e", "ł": "l", "ń": "n", "œ": "oe", "ś": "s",
    "š": "s", "ź": "z", "ż": "z", "ž": "z",
}
_SEP_RE = re.compile(r"[^a-z0-9]+")

def slugify(text: str, sep: str = "-", max_length: int | None = None) -> str:
    lowered = text.lower()
    mapped = "".join(CHAR_MAP.get(ch, ch) for ch in lowered)
    slug = _SEP_RE.sub(sep, mapped).strip(sep)
    if max_length is not None:
        slug = slug[:max_length].rstrip(sep)
    return slug

def unique_slug(text: str, existing: set[str], sep: str = "-") -> str:
    base = slugify(text, sep=sep)
    if base not in existing:
        return base
    n = 2
    while f"{base}{sep}{n}" in existing:
        n += 1
    return f"{base}{sep}{n}"

```python
import re

def canon(name):
    """Return the house-canonical form of a display name."""
    
    normalized_name = re.sub(r'\s+', ' ', name).strip()
    words = normalized_name.split()
    
    final_name_parts = []
    
    particles = {"de", "la", "van", "von", "di", "del", "della", "du", "da", "ter", "ten", "bin", "al", "der"}
    suffixes = {"jr", "sr", "ii", "iii", "iv", "v", "vi", "vii", "viii", "ix", "x"}
    
    i = 0
    while i < len(words):
        current_word = words[i]
        word_lower = current_word.lower()
        
        # Initial handling
        if (len(current_word) == 1 and current_word.isalpha()) or \
           (len(current_word) == 2 and current_word[0].isalpha() and current_word[1] == '.'):
            
            initial_group_chars = []
            j = i
            while j < len(words):
                next_word = words[j]
                next_word_char = next_word[0].upper() if next_word[0].isalpha() else ''

                if (len(next_word) == 1 and next_word.isalpha()) or \
                   (len(next_word) == 2 and next_word[0].isalpha() and next_word[1] == '.'):
                    initial_group_chars.append(next_word_char)
                    j += 1
                else:
                    break
            
            if initial_group_chars:
                final_name_parts.append(".".join(initial_group_chars) + ".")
                i = j - 1
            else:
                final_name_parts.append(current_word.capitalize()) 
        
        # "Mc" prefix
        elif word_lower.startswith("mc") and len(word_lower) > 2 and current_word[2:].isalpha():
             final_name_parts.append("Mc" + current_word[2:].capitalize())
        
        # Suffixes (Roman numerals are uppercase)
        elif word_lower in suffixes:
            final_name_parts.append(current_word.upper()) # Use current_word to preserve original case if already uppercase (e.g. JR)

        # Particles
        elif word_lower in particles and i > 0:
            final_name_parts.append(word_lower)

        # NEW RULE: Preserve ALLCAPS tokens if length > 1 (not an initial) and purely alphabetic
        elif len(current_word) > 1 and current_word.isalpha() and current_word.isupper():
            final_name_parts.append(current_word) # Preserve ALLCAPS

        # Default: Capitalize
        else:
            final_name_parts.append(current_word.capitalize())
        
        i += 1
        
    return " ".join(final_name_parts)

```

            initial_group_chars = []

                    j += 1

            if initial_group_chars:

                i = j - 1

                final_name_parts.append(current_word.capitalize()) 
        
        # "Mc" prefix logic remains the same

             final_name_parts.append("Mc" + current_word[2:].capitalize())

from decimal import Decimal, ROUND_HALF_EVEN


def round_money(amount):
    """Round a monetary amount to 2 decimal places using HALF_EVEN."""
    return float(Decimal(amount).quantize(Decimal("0.01"), rounding=ROUND_HALF_EVEN))


def line_amount(quantity, unit_price, discount_pct=0.0):
    """Net amount for a single invoice line after applying its discount."""
    gross = quantity * unit_price

"""slugforge core: transliteration table and slug helpers.

CHAR_MAP is generated from the transliteration source table in the ops repo
(tools/gen_charmap); regenerate it through the pipeline rather than editing
entries by hand. The slug helpers below the table are maintained normally.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re

CHAR_MAP = {
    "à": "a", "á": "a", "â": "a", "ã": "a", "ä": "a",
    "å": "a", "æ": "ae", "ç": "c", "è": "e", "é": "e",

    "ú": "u", "û": "u", "ü": "u", "ý": "y", "þ": "th",
    "ÿ": "y", "ß": "ss", "ć": "c", "č": "c", "đ": "d",
    "ę": "e", "ł": "l", "ń": "n", "œ": "oe", "ś": "s",
    "š": "s", "ź": "z", "ż": "z", "ž": "z",
}

_SEP_RE = re.compile(r"[^a-z0-9]+")


def slugify(text: str, sep: str = "-", max_length: int | None = None) -> str:
    """Build a URL-safe slug from arbitrary text.

    Lowercases, transliterates via CHAR_MAP, and collapses every run of
    non-alphanumeric characters into a single separator. ``max_length``
    truncates the result without leaving a dangling separator.
    """
    lowered = text.lower()
    mapped = "".join(CHAR_MAP.get(ch, ch) for ch in lowered)
    slug = _SEP_RE.sub(sep, mapped).strip(sep)
    if max_length is not None:
        slug = slug[:max_length].rstrip(sep)
    return slug


def unique_slug(text: str, existing: set[str], sep: str = "-") -> str:
    """Slugify ``text``, suffixing ``-2``, ``-3``, ... to avoid ``existing``."""
    base = slugify(text, sep=sep)
    if base not in existing:
        return base
    n = 2
    while f"{base}{sep}{n}" in existing:
        n += 1
    return f"{base}{sep}{n}"

"""slugforge core: transliteration table and slug helpers.

CHAR_MAP is generated from the transliteration source table in the ops repo
(tools/gen_charmap); regenerate it through the pipeline rather than editing
entries by hand. The slug helpers below the table are maintained normally.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re

CHAR_MAP = {
    "à": "a", "á": "a", "â": "a", "ã": "a", "ä": "a",
    "å": "a", "æ": "ae", "ç": "c", "è": "e", "é": "e",
    "ê": "e", "ë": "e", "ì": "i", "í": "i", "î": "i",
    "ï": "i", "ð": "d", "ñ": "n", "ò": "o", "ó": "o",
    "ô": "o", "õ": "o", "ö": "o", "ø": "o", "ù": "u",
    "ú": "u", "û": "u", "ü": "u", "ý": "y", "þ": "th",
    "ÿ": "y", "ß": "ss", "ć": "c", "č": "c", "đ": "d",
    "ę": "e", "ł": "l", "ń": "n", "œ": "oe", "ś": "s",
    "š": "s", "ź": "z", "ż": "z", "ž": "z",
}

_SEP_RE = re.compile(r"[^a-z0-9]+")


def slugify(text: str, sep: str = "-", max_length: int | None = None) -> str:
    """Build a URL-safe slug from arbitrary text.

    Lowercases, transliterates via CHAR_MAP, and collapses every run of
    non-alphanumeric characters into a single separator. ``max_length``
    truncates the result without leaving a dangling separator.
    """
    lowered = text.lower()
    mapped = "".join(CHAR_MAP.get(ch, ch) for ch in lowered)
    slug = _SEP_RE.sub(sep, mapped).strip(sep)
    if max_length is not None:
        slug = slug[:max_length].rstrip(sep)
    return slug


def unique_slug(text: str, existing: set[str], sep: str = "-") -> str:
    """Slugify ``text``, suffixing ``-2``, ``-3``, ... to avoid ``existing``."""
    base = slugify(text, sep=sep)
    if base not in existing:
        return base
    n = 2
    while f"{base}{sep}{n}" in existing:
        n += 1
    return f"{base}{sep}{n}"

After writing, read_file core.py to confirm it matches exactly (no stray quotes, the original CHAR_MAP, the set-based unique_slug), then run_tests. Note unique_slug must take (text, existing: set, sep) — NOT a Django queryset — because tests/test_unique.py imports it.

"""slugforge core: transliteration table and slug helpers.

CHAR_MAP is generated from the transliteration source table in the ops repo
(tools/gen_charmap); regenerate it through the pipeline rather than editing
entries by hand. The slug helpers below the table are maintained normally.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re

CHAR_MAP = {
    "à": "a", "á": "a", "â": "a", "ã": "a", "ä": "a",
    "å": "a", "æ": "ae", "ç": "c", "è": "e", "é": "e",
    "ê": "e", "ë": "e", "ì": "i", "í": "i", "î": "i",
    "ï": "i", "ð": "d", "ñ": "n", "ò": "o", "ó": "o",
    "ô": "o", "õ": "o", "ö": "o", "ø": "o", "ù": "u",
    "ú": "u", "û": "u", "ü": "u", "ý": "y", "þ": "th",
    "ÿ": "y", "ß": "ss", "ć": "c", "č": "c", "đ": "d",
    "ę": "e", "ł": "l", "ń": "n", "œ": "oe", "ś": "s",
    "š": "s", "ź": "z", "ż": "z", "ž": "z",
}

_SEP_RE = re.compile(r"[^a-z0-9]+")


def slugify(text: str, sep: str = "-", max_length: int | None = None) -> str:
    """Build a URL-safe slug from arbitrary text.

    Lowercases, transliterates via CHAR_MAP, and collapses every run of
    non-alphanumeric characters into a single separator. ``max_length``
    truncates the result without leaving a dangling separator.
    """
    lowered = text.lower()
    mapped = "".join(CHAR_MAP.get(ch, ch) for ch in lowered)
    slug = _SEP_RE.sub(sep, mapped).strip(sep)
    if max_length is not None:
        slug = slug[:max_length].rstrip(sep)
    return slug


def unique_slug(text: str, existing: set[str], sep: str = "-") -> str:
    """Slugify ``text``, suffixing ``-2``, ``-3``, ... to avoid ``existing``."""
    base = slugify(text, sep=sep)
    if base not in existing:
        return base
    n = 2
    while f"{base}{sep}{n}" in existing:
        n += 1
    return f"{base}{sep}{n}"

Stop and reset. You are massively overcomplicating this. There are NO snapshot tests, NO read-only files, and NO logical contradiction. The only test file is tests/test_render.py and it has 11 simple assert-equal tests. Ignore everything you've theorized.

The real bug is a one-line fix in escape_html: the replacement ORDER is wrong. It currently does < and > first, THEN &, so the ampersands it just inserted (in < / >) get double-escaped into &lt;. Replace & FIRST:

def escape_html(text):
    text = text.replace("&", "&")
    text = text.replace("<", "<").replace(">", ">")
    text = text.replace('"', """)
    return text

Apply exactly that change to mdlite.py (no inspect.stack, no regex lookaheads, no other changes), then run the tests. They will all pass. Do it now.
